paper_metadata.title: Static and Fatigue Properties of Rhenium-Alloyed Inconel 718 Produced by Powder Bed Fusion Additive Manufacturing

evidence.quote: Inconel 718 powder was coated with 3% wt. rhenium (In718-Re) using AM's in situ alloying capabilities to improve high-temperature properties.
Inconel 718 (In718), a Ni–Fe–Cr alloy modified with niobium, is renowned for its high strength, resistance to creep, and excellent fatigue properties at elevated temperatures up to 700 ◦C.
Inconel 718 powder was coated with 3% wt. rhenium (In718-Re) using AM's in situ alloying capabilities to improve high-temperature properties.
The representative as-built microstructure of the PBF-LB/M-fabricated In718-Re in a polished, non-etched state has been presented in Figure 2a.

process_steps.method: laser-based powder bed fusion of metals (PBF-LB/M)
process_steps.input_state: Inconel 718 powder with its surface modified by rhenium

evidence.quote: An SLM 250 system (Realizer, Germany) equipped with a 100 W fiber laser was used. The process parameters used were as follows: 50 µm layer thickness, 1200 µs scanning point time, 60 µm scanning point distance, and 160 µm hatch distance. The build platform was preheated to 250 °C prior to the process, and this temperature was maintained throughout the entire duration of the procedure.

parameters.cooling_method: Heating and cooling rates were maintained at 600 °C per hour

evidence.section: 2.3. Heat Treatment and Hot Isostatic Pressing Post-Treatment
evidence.quote: First, HIP was applied to reduce post-AM defects, with samples subjected to 1185 ◦C under 100 MPa pressure for 4 h. Heating and cooling rates were maintained at 600 ◦C per hour.

evidence.section: 2.3. Heat Treatment and Hot Isostatic Pressing Post-Treatment
evidence.quote: After HIP , the samples underwent solution annealing at 1100 ◦C in an argon atmosphere for 1 h, followed by rapid water cooling to retain the high-temperature microstructure and prevent precipitation of undesirable phases, such as σ or Laves. The heating rate for this stage was 200 ◦C per hour.

other.stage: first stage, for γ′′ phase formation

evidence.section: 2.3. Heat Treatment and Hot Isostatic Pressing Post-Treatment
evidence.quote: A two-stage artificial aging process followed to precipitate strengthening phases: 8 h at 718 ◦C for γ′′ phase formation and 10 h at 621 ◦C for γ′ phase formation, both in an argon protective atmosphere with a heating rate of 200 ◦C per hour. After aging, the samples were allowed to cool naturally in air.
